findings.pdf_says: Figure D.1 draws one tall brace "}" on the right-hand side of the flowchart. That single brace spans ALL THREE exit arrows -- the arrow leaving imperative-statement-1, the arrow leaving imperative-statement-2 and the arrow leaving imperative-statement-3 -- and the footnote reference "**" is printed to the right of the brace, vertically centred beside it. The footnote itself (page 1064) reads: "**   Each of these control transfers is to the end of the SEARCH statement unless the flow of control of the imperative-statement contains an EXIT, GO TO, GOBACK, or RETURN statement."
findings.markdown_says:
Condition-1 → True → imperative-statement-2 → **\*\***

(the brace is not rendered at all; the "**" marker appears only at the end of the imperative-statement-2 row, and the imperative-statement-1 row reads "→ True (AT END) * → imperative-statement-1 →" and the imperative-statement-3 row reads "\* Condition-2 → True → imperative-statement-3 * →", neither carrying "**")
findings.why_it_matters: The brace is the only thing that makes footnote ** apply to all three control transfers. With the brace dropped and "**" attached to a single row, the plural antecedent of "Each of these control transfers" disappears: a reader of the markdown concludes that only the imperative-statement-2 exit transfers to the end of the SEARCH statement, and that the AT END exit and the second WHEN exit are governed by something else. That is exactly the falsely-restrictive reading this sweep is looking for, applied to a figure grouping delimiter rather than a bracket.
findings.suggested_repair: Re-render the figure so the three exit arrows are shown as one group carrying the "**" marker, e.g. put "**" on its own line covering the three imperative-statement rows (or repeat "**" on each of the three exit arrows) instead of appending it to the imperative-statement-2 row only.

findings.pdf_says: D.3.2   Table definition   (a clause subordinate to "D.3   Tables and dynamic-length elementary items", printed in the same style and at the same numbering depth as "D.3.1   General")
findings.why_it_matters: D.3.1 is transcribed as "### D.3.1 General" (page 1057) but its sibling D.3.2 is transcribed at "##", the same level as its own parent "## D.3 Tables and dynamic-length elementary items". The markdown outline therefore shows D.3.2 as a peer of D.3 rather than a child of it, and D.3.1 as the only child. Any navigation, TOC generation or section-scoped citation built off the heading tree gets the wrong containment for the whole D.3 clause.
findings.suggested_repair: Demote to "### D.3.2 Table definition". The same one-level-too-shallow defect repeats for the remaining siblings of D.3.1: "## D.3.3 Values of tables" and "## D.3.4 References to table items" (page 1059), "## D.3.5 Subscripting" (page 1060) and "## D.3.6 Sorting tables" (page 1064) -- all should be "###" to match "### D.3.1 General".

findings.pdf_says: D.3.5.3   Subscripting example   (printed at the same numbering depth as "D.3.5.1   General" and "D.3.5.2   Subscripting using index-names")
findings.why_it_matters: Its two siblings are transcribed one level deeper -- "### D.3.5.1 General" and "### D.3.5.2 Subscripting using index-names" (page 1060) -- while D.3.5.3 sits at "##", the same level as their shared parent "## D.3.5 Subscripting". The markdown outline therefore detaches D.3.5.3 (and the SEARCH example that follows it) from the Subscripting clause that contains it.
findings.suggested_repair: Demote to "### D.3.5.3 Subscripting example", and likewise demote "## D.3.5.4 SEARCH example" (page 1063) to "###", so all four D.3.5.x subclauses sit at one consistent level under D.3.5.
